nodes.label: H0b: Native centre selection suppression
nodes.rationale: Active test to explain doubled/native-looking brackets and stale inspector text by clearing KEX native centre object/hover/frob globals.

nodes.label: H1: HMD-owned KEX camera baseline
nodes.rationale: Active baseline to explain culling/picking issues when visible RenderView and native KEX camera differ.

nodes.label: H2: UI and world interaction domain routing
nodes.rationale: Active hypothesis explaining why inventory cursor can interact with world objects and UI/world ray selection conflicts.

nodes.label: H3: Weapon/projectile direction sink
nodes.rationale: Active diagnostic for weapon firing paths; identifies FUN_1403eedd0 as a strong hitscan aim-takeover lead.

nodes.label: H4: True world selection via controller-origin ray
nodes.rationale: Active hypothesis addressing parallax problems and flat-pixel tuning failures by using filtered KEX traces or controller rays.

nodes.label: H4b: VR-native selection brackets
nodes.rationale: Evolving hypothesis that selection brackets should ride on the DLL OpenXR layer fed by Squirrel targets to fix spatial alignment.

nodes.label: H6C: Smooth analog turn via KEX accumulator
nodes.rationale: Active diagnostic to fix snap discontinuities and flash frames by feeding KEX's normal camera accumulator.

nodes.label: H6B: Tracking discomfort and camera chase
nodes.rationale: Active diagnostic explaining pitch stepping/lag as KEX mouse-delta and pitch-servo update quantization.

nodes.label: H6D: Pair-lock stereo prediction
nodes.rationale: Active diagnostic for alternate-eye stereo latency; suggests predicting two frames ahead for the first eye.

nodes.label: H8: Native controller locomotion
nodes.rationale: Design direction to migrate from keyboard emulation to KEX-native controls for analog joystick magnitude.

nodes.label: H9: Weapon model takeover via attach state
nodes.rationale: Static/live RE lead suggesting first-person visuals are retargeted via attachment state rather than D3D draw edits.

nodes.label: H10: Central pose snapshot and semantic rays
nodes.rationale: Architecture hypothesis to reduce axis/domain bugs by centralizing VR-to-world conversion.

nodes.label: H11: Vanilla Options influence
nodes.rationale: Active hypothesis that vanilla settings (Smoothing, HUD Scale) affect VR comfort and aim paths.

nodes.label: H12: Unified metres-to-KEX scale
nodes.rationale: Active diagnostic to drive translation, rays, and IPD from a single world_scale (baseline 3.28).

nodes.label: H13: AE Squirrel weapon layer handoff
nodes.rationale: High-confidence hypothesis that Squirrel CameraObj control is the preferred route for viewmodel and projectile aim.

nodes.label: FUN_1403eedd0
nodes.rationale: Identified as the strongest pistol/hitscan aim-takeover lead performing per-weapon shot setup.

nodes.label: FUN_1404574c0
nodes.rationale: Broad collision/trace function; targeted for detour to rewrite trace end points for specific aim callers.

nodes.label: CameraObj
nodes.rationale: AE Squirrel object used for viewmodel control; confirmed as the surface for weapon rotation and translation.

nodes.label: ss2vr_interact.nut
nodes.rationale: Squirrel script for semantic object interaction using ND.FullRayTest.

nodes.label: ss2vr_weapon_probe.nut
nodes.rationale: Squirrel script for viewmodel pose bridge and projectile re-aiming.

nodes.label: H14: VR Melee Native Drive
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that VR melee should drive native engine actions rather than custom collision for the first pass.

nodes.label: H15: Main-menu VR Control
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that main menu control should use a controller ray pointer rather than gameplay navigation hijacking.

nodes.label: H16: Skill Spread and Recoil
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis regarding how skill-based spread and recoil are affected by VR aim takeover and HMD reassertion.

nodes.label: H17: VR Tonal Feedback
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that VR visual effects should be implemented as an OpenXR layer.

nodes.label: H19: LGMD Face Deletion
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that direct deletion of mesh faces can produce clean VR viewmodels while preserving animations.

nodes.label: H21: Manual Reloads
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that manual reloads can be implemented via gesture detection dispatching native commands.

nodes.label: H22: Virtual Holsters
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that holsters can work as inferred-body spatial command slots.

nodes.label: H23: Object Grabbing/Throwing
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that Squirrel can support physics-based grabbing and throwing.

nodes.label: H24: Long Weapon Support Grip
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that two-handed weapons can use a primary right-hand pose with a left-hand support constraint.

nodes.label: H26: HUD Curvature
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that HUD/Inventory should use an OpenXR cylinder layer for comfort.

nodes.label: H27: Native Shock Overlay Rects
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that native engine overlay rectangles can replace hardcoded HUD panel slices.

nodes.label: H31: Viewmodel pose bleed is from CameraObj-frame patching
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that viewmodel rotation/translation bleed is caused by the layer where CameraObj is patched rather than projectile aim logic.

nodes.label: H33: First-pass LGMM/LGPMNM import is sufficient for posing/exporting a static wrench-hand source
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis regarding the viability of using LGPMNM payloads for static weapon viewmodel authoring.

nodes.label: H34: Nemyax-style node rebuild may make full stock weapon subobject pruning viable
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that specific node hierarchy shapes (Nemyax-style) prevent crashes when pruning subobjects from animated weapons.

nodes.label: H35: Static LGMD mirror can make an empty right-hand model from the live left hand
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that binary-level mirroring of LGMD files can produce valid right-hand models from left-hand sources.

nodes.label: KPF v1.47
nodes.rationale: Version that partially falsified H31 and introduced roll-sign regressions.

nodes.label: KPF v1.48
nodes.rationale: Version fixing the roll-sign regression identified in v1.47.
